public_nodes.title: What is a CSV file?
public_nodes.body: A CSV (comma-separated values) file stores tabular data as plain text. Each row is a record; fields within a row are separated by commas. CSV files can be opened in any spreadsheet application.

public_nodes.title: Difference between text and number data types
public_nodes.body: Numeric cells support arithmetic; text cells do not. Dates stored as text cannot be sorted chronologically. Always check the data type before calculating totals.

public_nodes.title: What is a pivot table?
public_nodes.body: A pivot table summarises rows by grouping and aggregating (sum, count, average). It lets you quickly explore large datasets without writing formulas.

public_nodes.title: Why use the median instead of the mean for skewed data?
public_nodes.body: The mean is pulled toward outliers. If a dataset contains a few very large values, the mean will be higher than the typical value. The median splits the sorted dataset in half and is unaffected by extreme values.

public_nodes.title: What does standard deviation tell you?
public_nodes.body: Standard deviation measures how spread out values are from the mean. A small SD means values cluster near the mean; a large SD means they are widely dispersed.

public_nodes.title: What is a frequency distribution?
public_nodes.body: A frequency distribution counts how many times each value (or value range) appears. A histogram is its visual equivalent.

public_nodes.title: How do you spot an outlier?
public_nodes.body: A common rule: values more than 1.5 times the interquartile range below Q1 or above Q3 are candidate outliers. Always investigate before removing; outliers sometimes reflect real events.

public_nodes.title: When should you use a bar chart vs a line chart?
public_nodes.body: Use a bar chart when comparing discrete categories (e.g. sales by region). Use a line chart when showing a continuous trend over time (e.g. monthly revenue).

public_nodes.title: What is a scatter plot used for?
public_nodes.body: A scatter plot shows the relationship between two numeric variables. If the points form a rising pattern, the variables are positively correlated.

public_nodes.title: Why can dual-axis charts mislead?
public_nodes.body: Dual-axis charts use two different y-scales, which can make weak correlations look strong. The reader may assume both series are directly comparable when they are not.

public_nodes.title: How do you handle missing values?
public_nodes.body: Options: delete rows with missing values, fill with a default (mean, median, most common), or mark them as unknown. The right choice depends on how many rows are missing and why the data is absent.

public_nodes.title: What is deduplication?
public_nodes.body: Deduplication identifies and removes exact or near-identical rows. Always confirm why duplicates exist before deleting; sometimes they are legitimate repeated events.

public_nodes.title: What is data normalisation?
public_nodes.body: Normalisation standardises the range of values so that one variable does not dominate others. Common methods: min-max scaling, z-score standardisation.

public_nodes.title: What does SELECT * FROM do?
public_nodes.body: SELECT * FROM table_name returns every column and every row from the specified table. Add a WHERE clause to filter rows.

public_nodes.title: How does a WHERE clause work?
public_nodes.body: WHERE filters rows based on a condition: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE department = 'Sales'. Multiple conditions can be combined with AND / OR.

public_nodes.title: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN?
public_nodes.body: INNER JOIN returns only rows that match in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table, with NULLs where the right table has no match.

public_nodes.title: How do you read a CSV file in Python with pandas?
public_nodes.body: Use pd.read_csv('filename.csv'). The result is a DataFrame with columns matching the CSV headers. Check df.head() to inspect the first five rows.

public_nodes.title: What is a pandas DataFrame?
public_nodes.body: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional table with labelled rows and columns, similar to a spreadsheet. Each column is a Series of uniform type.

public_nodes.title: How do you filter rows in a DataFrame?
public_nodes.body: Use a boolean mask: df[df['age'] > 30]. This returns a new DataFrame with only the rows where age exceeds 30.

public_nodes.title: How do you plot a simple chart from pandas data?
public_nodes.body: df['column'].plot(kind='bar') creates a bar chart using matplotlib under the hood. Call plt.show() to display it.

public_nodes.title: What is the difference between Python lists and pandas Series?
public_nodes.body: A list is a general-purpose Python container with no type constraint. A Series is a labelled, single-type array optimised for vectorised operations and alignment.
